intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Sunrise Temple Complex Tour
experiences.description: Explore the magnificent 12th-century Khmer temple complex at sunrise, wandering through Angkor Wat, Bayon, and Ta Prohm. Hire a local tuk-tuk driver for a full-day small circuit tour to witness the iconic reflection of the towers in the moat and discover intricate bas-relief carvings depicting Hindu mythology.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Genocide Memorial & Royal Palace Visit
experiences.description: Spend a deeply moving and culturally enriching day visiting the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) to understand Cambodia's tragic Khmer Rouge history, followed by a visit to the stunning Silver Pagoda and Royal Palace complex showcasing traditional Khmer architecture and royal artifacts.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Escape
experiences.description: Take a ferry to the pristine white-sand beaches of Koh Rong Samloem island, where crystal-clear turquoise waters and untouched jungle meet. Snorkel among vibrant coral reefs, kayak through mangroves, and witness bioluminescent plankton glowing in the sea after dark for an unforgettable natural spectacle.

experiences.name: Siem Reap Khmer Cooking Class & Market Tour
experiences.description: Join a hands-on Khmer cooking class beginning with a guided tour of the vibrant Psar Leu local market to select fresh ingredients like lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime. Learn to prepare traditional dishes including Fish Amok, Lok Lak, and mango salad under the guidance of a local chef in a traditional open-air kitchen.
experiences.location: Old Market Area (Psar Chas), Siem Reap

experiences.name: Kampot River Sunset Kayaking & Pepper Farm Tour
experiences.description: Paddle along the serene Kampot River through lush mangroves and past French colonial architecture as the sun sets over the Elephant Mountains. Visit a renowned Kampot pepper farm to learn about the world-famous cultivation process, sample fresh green and red peppercorns, and enjoy a riverside dinner at a local restaurant.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into Boutique Stay in Angkor Archaeological Park area. After settling in, take a leisurely walk around the local neighborhood near your guesthouse. Visit the Angkor Night Market area during daylight to get oriented, browse local handicraft stalls, and pick up a SIM card from a nearby shop for cheap local data.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Pub Street and the Old Market (Phsar Chas) area in Siem Reap town center (~15 min tuk-tuk from Angkor area). Soak in the vibrant street atmosphere, watch local performers, and enjoy your first taste of Cambodian street food.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick $2–3 banh mi sandwich or noodle soup from a street vendor near your guesthouse after check-in.
meals.dinner: Khmer Kitchen Restaurant on Pub Street — try Amok (fish curry) and fried rice for around $4–6 per person. Very popular with budget travelers.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some USD to KHR (Cambodian Riel) at the airport or a local money changer for small purchases. Cambodia widely accepts USD. Tuk-tuk from airport to Angkor area costs around $8–10. Negotiate in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn (4:30 AM) for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise. Watch the temple reflect in the lotus pond as the sun rises — one of the most breathtaking sights in Southeast Asia. Spend the early morning exploring Angkor Wat's outer galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Hindu epic Mahabharata, and the central towers. Buy a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62) at the ticket booth the evening before or early morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or cycle (rent a bicycle for $2–3/day) to Angkor Thom complex. Explore the massive South Gate with its stone face carvings, the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon Temple, and the Terrace of the Elephants. Take a shaded rest during peak heat (12–2 PM).
day_by_day.evening: Return to guesthouse to freshen up. Head to Siem Reap's Old Market area for dinner and evening exploration. Browse the night market for affordable souvenirs like scarves and wood carvings.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks (bananas, baguette) from a nearby stall the night before for the sunrise visit. Grab a $1 Cambodian iced coffee from a cart near the temple entrance.
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the local food stalls just outside the Angkor Thom South Gate — rice with grilled pork or lok lak (beef stir-fry) for $2–4.
meals.dinner: Try Bugs Cafe or a local Khmer restaurant on Sivatha Street. A full meal with rice, soup, and a drink costs $4–7.

day_by_day.notes: Start the sunrise visit as early as 4:30–5:00 AM. Bring a flashlight or phone torch for the dark walk to the reflecting pond. Wear light, breathable clothing and bring sunscreen and a reusable water bottle. Angkor Wat alone can take 3–4 hours to explore properly.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Ta Prohm Temple — famously known as the 'Tomb Raider temple' — where massive tree roots engulf ancient stone walls. Arrive early (7–8 AM) before tour groups arrive for the best photos and a more peaceful atmosphere. Then visit Banteay Kdei, a Buddhist monastery temple nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle or take a tuk-tuk to Srah Srang, a royal bathing pool with a beautiful terrace. Then head to Pre Rup, a 10th-century Hindu temple-mountain with great views from the top. Visit Banteay Samré, a well-preserved but less-visited temple that offers a quieter experience.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Angkor Centre for Conservation of Biodiversity (ACCB) if open, or head into town for a traditional Apsara dance performance. The Smile of Angkor show or a free performance at a local restaurant offers cultural insight into Khmer classical dance.

meals.breakfast: Eat at your guesthouse if breakfast is included, or try a local $1.50 rice porridge (bobor) from a street cart near the temple area.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near Srah Srang — buy fresh fruit, sticky rice, and grilled skewers from mobile vendors for under $3.
meals.dinner: Genevieve's Restaurant or Chamkar Vegetarian Restaurant in town — budget-friendly Khmer and vegetarian options from $3–6.

day_by_day.notes: Ta Prohm gets very crowded by 9–10 AM. Arriving early is essential. Wear closed-toe shoes as temple roots and uneven stones can be tricky. Stay hydrated — November can still be warm and humid.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Banteay Srei Temple (~35 km from Siem Reap). Known as the 'Citadel of Women,' this 10th-century temple features extraordinarily intricate pink sandstone carvings — considered the finest in all of Angkor. Hire a tuk-tuk for the day (negotiate $15–20 for a full-day trip). On the way, stop at Banteay Samré if not visited yesterday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Landmine Museum (Aki Ra's Museum) near Banteay Srei — a deeply moving and educational experience about Cambodia's tragic history with landmines and the ongoing demining efforts. Entry is $5 and supports the cause. Then stop at Kbal Spean (River of a Thousand Lingas) if energy allows — a 1.5 km jungle hike to ancient riverbed carvings.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap. Visit Angkor Night Market for souvenir shopping. Enjoy a traditional Khmer massage ($7–10/hour) at one of the many reputable massage parlors on Sivatha Street — a great way to relax after days of temple walking.

meals.breakfast: Eat a hearty breakfast before the day trip — try a $2 egg baguette or pancake from a street vendor near the guesthouse.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local village restaurant near Banteay Srei — simple Khmer dishes like fried rice with egg or noodle soup for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Haven Restaurant (social enterprise training restaurant) — excellent Khmer food at $5–8 per dish, supporting at-risk youth. Book ahead if possible.

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is a UNESCO highlight and should not be missed. The road can be dusty — bring a scarf or mask. The Landmine Museum is sobering but essential for understanding modern Cambodian history. Tuk-tuk drivers often double as informal guides — tipping $1–2 is appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Siem Reap town itself. Visit the Angkor National Museum ($12 entry) for an excellent overview of Khmer civilization, history, and the Angkor empire — great context if you haven't visited yet. Then walk through the colorful Old Market (Phsar Chas) to browse local produce, spices, and crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat trip on Tonlé Sap Lake (~15 km south of Siem Reap). This is one of Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lakes and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. See floating villages where entire communities live on the water — schools, churches, and shops all afloat. Boat trips cost around $10–15 per person from the Chong Kneas or Kampong Phluk docks.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free cooking demonstration or join a budget cooking class ($15–25) at a local school like Le Tigre de Papier — learn to make Amok, lok lak, and fresh spring rolls.

meals.breakfast: Try a traditional Khmer breakfast of num banh chok (rice noodles with green curry fish sauce) from a local market stall for $1–2.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local restaurant near the Old Market — fish soup or grilled chicken with rice for $3–4.
meals.dinner: Cook your own dinner if you took the cooking class, or eat at a local spot near Pub Street for $4–6.

day_by_day.notes: Tonlé Sap Lake visits are best in November as water levels are still high from rainy season, making the floating villages more accessible and photogenic. Kampong Phluk is more authentic and less touristy than Chong Kneas — ask your tuk-tuk driver to take you there instead.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a bus from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (5–6 hours, $6–10 with Giant Ibis or Mekong Express — highly recommended for safety and comfort). Book tickets the day before. Depart around 7–8 AM to arrive by early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh. Check into a budget guesthouse near the riverfront (Riverside area has many options for $8–15/night). After settling in, walk along the Sisowath Quay (riverfront promenade) and visit the Royal Palace ($10 entry) and the Silver Pagoda — stunning examples of Khmer royal architecture with gilded spires.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively riverfront area. Watch the sunset over the Mekong and Tonlé Sap confluence from the promenade. Browse street food carts and enjoy the local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure — grab a $1.50 baguette with pâté (French colonial influence) from a street vendor near the bus station.
meals.lunch: Eat on the bus or at a roadside stop — vendors sell rice boxes and snacks for $1–2.
meals.dinner: Eat at a local Khmer restaurant near the riverfront — try kuy teav (noodle soup) or bai sach chrouk (pork and rice) for $2–4.

day_by_day.notes: Giant Ibis bus is slightly pricier but significantly safer and more reliable than cheaper alternatives — worth the extra $2–3. Book online at giantibis.com. Store valuables in your day bag, not overhead bins, on the bus.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge prison where an estimated 17,000 people were tortured and killed between 1975–1979. Entry is $5. This is an emotionally heavy but historically essential experience. Allow 2–3 hours and approach with respect.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk (~$5 each way) to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields (~15 km from city center). Walk the peaceful memorial grounds, listen to the audio guide ($3 extra — highly recommended), and pay respects at the memorial stupa containing thousands of skulls. A deeply moving and important site for understanding Cambodia's recent history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the riverfront to decompress. Visit Wat Phnom — the city's namesake hilltop temple — at dusk when it's beautifully lit. Then enjoy a quiet dinner and reflect on the day's experiences.

meals.breakfast: Eat at your guesthouse or a nearby café — eggs, toast, and coffee for $2–3.
meals.lunch: Eat near Tuol Sleng at a local restaurant — simple rice and curry for $3.
meals.dinner: Friends Restaurant (social enterprise) near the riverfront — excellent Khmer tapas and Western fusion, supporting street youth. Budget $6–10.

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally draining. Pace yourself, take breaks, and be respectful of the space. Photography is allowed but be mindful. Combined, these two sites take a full day. Dress modestly.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco dome market built in 1937. Browse stalls selling jewelry, clothing, electronics, and local produce. Then visit the National Museum of Cambodia ($5 entry) — home to the world's largest collection of Khmer art, including pre-Angkorian sculptures and artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel day: Take a bus or shared taxi from Phnom Penh to Kampot (~3 hours, $6–8). Kampot is a charming riverside colonial town and the gateway to Cambodia's southern coast. Check into a budget guesthouse ($8–12/night). Explore the old French colonial town center on foot — beautiful crumbling architecture along quiet streets.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Kampot River — many guesthouses and tour operators offer $5–8 sunset boat trips with drinks. Watch fireflies emerge after dark along the riverbanks — a magical experience unique to Kampot.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a local Phnom Penh café — bánh mì or rice porridge for $1.50–2.50.
meals.lunch: Grab food at the bus station or from a roadside vendor during the journey.
meals.dinner: Eat at Epic Arts Café or Rusty Keyhole in Kampot — budget-friendly Western and Khmer food from $4–7, with great riverside atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is famous for its pepper — one of the world's finest. Pick up a small bag at a local shop as a souvenir ($3–5). The town is very walkable and has a relaxed, laid-back vibe — a welcome change from the intensity of Phnom Penh.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a motorbike ($5–7/day) or bicycle ($2–3/day) and explore the Kampot countryside. Visit Bokor National Park — a scenic mountain drive (25 km) to the abandoned French hill station at 1,000m elevation. See the eerie ruins of the old Bokor Palace Hotel, a Catholic church, and stunning views over the Gulf of Thailand on clear days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kep (~25 km from Kampot) — a former French colonial seaside resort town. Visit the famous Kep Crab Market and walk along the small but charming Kep Beach. The beach is modest but the seafood is exceptional. Explore the ruined villas left from the Khmer Rouge era — haunting reminders of Cambodia's past.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot for the evening. Walk along the riverside promenade, visit a local bar for a $0.50–1 Angkor draft beer, and enjoy the relaxed small-town atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat at your guesthouse or a local café — try a Kampot pepper egg omelette with baguette for $2–3.
meals.lunch: At Kep Crab Market — fresh steamed crab with Kampot pepper sauce ($5–8 for a whole crab) and grilled seafood skewers. A must-eat experience.
meals.dinner: Eat at a local Kampot restaurant — Khmer curry or amok with rice for $3–5.

day_by_day.notes: The road to Bokor can be steep and winding — only ride a motorbike if you're comfortable with mountain roads. Otherwise, hire a tuk-tuk for the day ($15–20). The crab at Kep is the highlight of the south coast — budget a little extra for this meal. November weather should be dry and pleasant in the south.

day_by_day.morning: Optional: Take an early morning trip to Phnom Chhngok Cave Temple — a stunning 7th-century Khmer temple hidden inside a large cave (~8 km from Kampot). Entry $1. Explore the cave, see ancient brick shrines, and enjoy the surrounding countryside. Alternatively, visit a Kampot pepper farm for a free or low-cost tour to learn about the famous spice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure plans: if flying from Phnom Penh, take the afternoon bus back ($6–8, 3 hours). If flying from Sihanoukville, take a short bus or taxi (~1.5 hours, $5). Use any remaining time to do final souvenir shopping in Kampot's local market — pick up Kampot pepper, palm sugar, and local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Cambodia — celebrate with a proper sit-down Khmer dinner. Reflect on 10 incredible days of temples, history, culture, and coastal beauty. Pack and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast — num banh chok (rice noodles with fish curry) or a local café breakfast for $1.50–3.
meals.lunch: Eat light before travel — grab street food or a quick rice dish for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last night — a proper Khmer set meal with amok, lok lak, and fresh spring rolls at a mid-range local restaurant for $8–12 total.

day_by_day.notes: Final budget summary estimate for 10 days: Accommodation $80–130, Food $80–120, Transport $50–70, Entry fees $50–70, Activities $30–50. Total estimated trip cost: $290–440 USD excluding flights. Cambodia is one of Southeast Asia's most rewarding and affordable destinations — the combination of world-class history, vibrant culture, and emerging beach scenes makes it exceptional value.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and freshen up after your flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. Take a gentle orientation stroll around the hotel grounds and nearby Siem Reap Old Market (Phsar Chas) area to get your bearings, pick up a SIM card, and exchange currency.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Pub Street and the surrounding Night Market on foot. Browse local handicrafts, silk scarves, and Khmer souvenirs. Enjoy the lively atmosphere as a low-key introduction to Siem Reap.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Eat at the airport or grab a quick bite near the hotel upon arrival — try a local noodle soup (kuy teav) from a street stall near Old Market for ~$2–3.
meals.dinner: Mahob Restaurant (near Old Market) — a mid-range Khmer restaurant serving traditional amok fish curry, lok lak beef, and fresh spring rolls. Budget ~$10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: November is the tail end of the rainy season in Cambodia — expect warm, mostly dry weather with occasional short showers. Pack a light rain jacket. Stay hydrated after your flight. Rest early to prepare for full days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise (arrive by 05:30). Watch the temple's reflection shimmer in the lotus pond as the sky turns gold and pink — one of Southeast Asia's most breathtaking moments. Explore the outer galleries and bas-reliefs depicting the Hindu epic Mahabharata after sunrise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Angkor Wat's inner sanctum and central towers. Then visit the nearby Angkor Thom complex — enter through the South Gate flanked by 54 stone deities, and spend time at the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces. Walk through the Baphuon and Terrace of the Elephants.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap town. Visit the Artisans Angkor workshop (free entry) to watch craftspeople carving stone and lacquerware, keeping ancient Khmer traditions alive. Browse their fair-trade shop.

meals.breakfast: Early light snack from hotel or street vendor before sunrise — a banana and coffee to go.
meals.lunch: Blue Pumpkin Café inside Angkor Archaeological Park area — sandwiches, salads, and fresh juices in a cool air-conditioned setting. ~$6–9 per person.
meals.dinner: Cuisine Wat Damnak — a celebrated mid-range Khmer tasting menu restaurant in Siem Reap. Book in advance. ~$25–30 per person for a set menu of seasonal Cambodian dishes.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Archaeological Park Pass (~$62 USD) — it covers multiple temple visits over 3 days and is the best value for this itinerary. Hire a tuk-tuk driver for the day (~$15–20) for convenient temple hopping. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ta Prohm — the famous 'jungle temple' where massive silk-cotton tree roots embrace ancient stone walls. Made iconic by the Tomb Raider film, this UNESCO site offers extraordinary photo opportunities and a mystical atmosphere. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Banteay Srei, a smaller but exquisitely detailed 10th-century temple carved in pink sandstone, located ~35 km north of Siem Reap. Its intricate carvings of devatas and mythological scenes are considered the finest in all of Angkor. Stop at the Landmine Museum on the way back to learn about Cambodia's painful history with unexploded ordnance.
day_by_day.evening: Attend an Apsara Dance performance — a classical Khmer dance form listed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list. Several restaurants offer dinner-and-show packages. Recommended: Smile of Angkor or Apsara Theatre.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery — try nom pang (Cambodian baguette sandwich) from a street vendor for $1–2.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from a local market near Banteay Srei, or eat at a simple local restaurant in the village nearby. Budget ~$4–6.
meals.dinner: Apsara dinner show package — includes a buffet of Khmer dishes (amok, lok lak, papaya salad) plus the performance. ~$18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Hire the same tuk-tuk driver for continuity — negotiate a full-day rate (~$20–25 for distant temples). Banteay Srei requires an additional tuk-tuk journey of about 45 minutes each way. The Landmine Museum is sobering but highly educational — a $5 donation is suggested.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Preah Khan — a sprawling, largely unrestored temple complex that feels like a true jungle adventure. Explore its long corridors, stone libraries, and tree-root-covered walls with far fewer crowds than Ta Prohm. Then head to Neak Pean, an artificial island temple set in a pond, accessible via a wooden walkway.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat trip on Tonlé Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Visit a floating village (Kampong Phluk or Chong Khneas) to see how thousands of Cambodians live on water year-round, with stilted houses, floating schools, and fish farms.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and wander through Siem Reap's vibrant Night Market. Enjoy a traditional Khmer massage (~$8–12/hour) at one of the reputable wellness centers along Sivatha Boulevard.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Eat at a floating restaurant on Tonlé Sap Lake — fresh grilled fish and rice dishes. ~$6–8 per person.
meals.dinner: Haven Restaurant — a social enterprise training at-risk youth in hospitality. Excellent Western and Khmer fusion dishes. ~$10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is Day 3 of the Angkor Pass — use it for Preah Khan and Neak Pean in the morning. The Tonlé Sap boat trip costs ~$15–20 per person including a guide. Book through your hotel or a reputable tour operator. November water levels are still high, making the floating village experience particularly immersive.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siem Reap by private minivan or bus to Phnom Penh (~5–6 hours). Book in advance with Giant Ibis or Mekong Express for comfortable, reliable service (~$12–15). Enjoy the Cambodian countryside scenery en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh early-to-mid afternoon. Check in to your mid-range hotel (recommended: Pavilion Hotel or Mad Monkey Hostel Boutique). Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — a dazzling complex of golden spires, sacred Buddha statues, and a floor made of 5,000 silver tiles. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Riverside Promenade (Sisowath Quay) as the sun sets over the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers. Watch local families picnic, children play, and monks walk in saffron robes — a quintessential Phnom Penh evening scene.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab nom pang before the bus.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or eat at a rest stop along the highway — local rice dishes for ~$3–5.
meals.dinner: Friends the Restaurant (Phnom Penh) — another social enterprise training street youth. Excellent tapas-style Khmer and fusion dishes. ~$10–14 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Royal Palace closes at 17:00, so time your arrival accordingly. Phnom Penh is a bustling capital — keep valuables secure, especially along the riverside. Tuk-tuks and Grab (ride-hailing app) are the best ways to get around the city.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge detention center where up to 17,000 people were imprisoned and tortured between 1975–1979. A deeply moving and essential part of understanding Cambodia's modern history. Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial (~15 km from city center) — the most significant of Cambodia's 300+ killing fields. The audio guide (included in the $6 entry fee) is narrated by survivors and is profoundly powerful. Pay respects at the Memorial Stupa containing 8,000 skulls. Return to the city and visit the National Museum of Cambodia — housing the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Phnom Penh Night Market (Phsar Reatrey) for street food, local goods, and live music. Alternatively, visit a rooftop bar overlooking the Mekong for sunset cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Romdeng Restaurant — a social enterprise serving traditional Cambodian cuisine including regional specialties. ~$10–14 per person.
meals.dinner: Street food at the Night Market — grilled corn, fried noodles, fresh spring rolls, sugar cane juice. ~$4–7 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — allow time to process. These sites are essential for understanding Cambodia but may not be suitable for very young children. Dress respectfully. The National Museum closes at 17:00.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Wat Phnom — the hilltop temple that gives Phnom Penh its name. Dating to 1373, it's the spiritual heart of the city. Watch monks chant morning prayers and observe locals making offerings. Then explore the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — an Art Deco yellow dome housing stalls of gold jewelry, silks, electronics, and fresh produce.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a scenic boat trip on the Mekong River from Phnom Penh to see the confluence of the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers (called Chaktomuk — 'Four Faces'). Visit Silk Island (Koh Dach) by boat (~20 minutes) — a peaceful island where traditional silk weaving is practiced by local families. Watch weavers at their looms and shop directly from artisans.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Phnom Penh by bus or minivan to Kampot (~3 hours, ~$8–10 with Giant Ibis or Cambodian Smile). Arrive in Kampot and check in to a riverside guesthouse (recommended: Rikitikitavi or Greenhouse Kampot).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on Silk Island — simple local restaurant serving grilled fish and rice. ~$5–7.
meals.dinner: Rikitikitavi Restaurant, Kampot — a beloved riverside institution serving Khmer and Western dishes with a view of the Kampot River. ~$8–12 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is a charming, laid-back colonial town on the Kampot River, famous for its pepper plantations and proximity to the coast. November weather here is warm and mostly dry — ideal for outdoor exploration. Book your guesthouse in advance as Kampot has grown in popularity.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or motorbike (~$3–8/day) and explore the Kampot countryside. Visit a Kampot Pepper Farm — Kampot pepper is a UNESCO-protected Geographical Indication product and among the world's finest. Tour the plantation, taste different pepper varieties (red, black, white, green), and buy directly from farmers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Bokor National Park via a winding mountain road (~30 km). Explore the abandoned French colonial hill station — the eerie Bokor Palace Hotel, the old casino, and a church, all left to the jungle since the 1970s. Enjoy panoramic views over the Gulf of Thailand and the plains below. The site has a haunting, cinematic quality.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot. Enjoy a sunset kayak or boat trip on the Kampot River — watch fireflies begin to appear as dusk falls (Kampot is famous for its firefly displays along the mangrove-lined riverbanks).

meals.breakfast: Café Espresso or a local bakery in Kampot town — croissant, eggs, and coffee. ~$4–6.
meals.lunch: Picnic or simple lunch near Bokor — bring snacks or eat at the park's basic café.
meals.dinner: Epic Arts Café, Kampot — a social enterprise run by and for people with disabilities. Excellent pizza, burgers, and Khmer dishes. ~$7–10 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Bokor National Park entry fee is ~$5. A motorbike is the best way to explore — the road to Bokor is paved but steep and winding. The firefly boat trip costs ~$8–12 per person through local operators. Kampot's riverside is magical at night — linger over dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short tuk-tuk or shared taxi to Kep (~25 minutes, ~$5–8). Kep is a tiny, sleepy seaside town with a fascinating colonial past and Cambodia's best crab market. Visit the famous Kep Crab Market — a string of seafood shacks on stilts over the water where you can watch fishermen bring in their catch. Order fresh Kampot pepper crab cooked right in front of you.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on Kep Beach or take a short boat trip (~$5) to Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) — a beautiful, largely undeveloped island with white sand beaches, clear water, and simple beach bungalows. Swim, snorkel, and sunbathe in a tranquil setting with no cars or crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kep or Kampot by late afternoon. Enjoy a slow, relaxing evening along the Kampot riverside — browse bookshops, sip cocktails, and watch the sun set over the river.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Kampot.
meals.lunch: Kep Crab Market — fresh Kampot pepper crab, grilled prawns, and seafood rice. ~$10–15 per person (a must-try experience).
meals.dinner: Rusty Keyhole, Kampot — a popular riverside bar and restaurant with great cocktails, burgers, and Khmer dishes. ~$8–12 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Rabbit Island boat trips depart from Kep Beach — last boats return around 17:00, so time accordingly. Kep is very small and best explored on foot or by bicycle. The combination of Kep's crab market and Rabbit Island makes this one of the trip's most memorable days — a perfect blend of culture, food, and beach.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kampot — enjoy a leisurely breakfast by the river. Take one last stroll through Kampot's charming colonial Old Town, admiring the French-era shophouses painted in pastel colors. Visit a local coffee shop and try Cambodian iced coffee (café touk doh ko) — strong drip coffee over condensed milk and ice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Kampot for Phnom Penh by bus or minivan (~3 hours). Depending on your onward flight time, either head directly to Phnom Penh International Airport or spend a couple of hours doing last-minute souvenir shopping at the Russian Market (Phsar Tuol Tom Poung) — the best market in Phnom Penh for silk, handicrafts, clothing, and antiques at fair prices.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Cambodia from Phnom Penh International Airport, or overnight in Phnom Penh if your flight is the following day. Reflect on 10 extraordinary days of temples, history, culture, river life, and coastline.

meals.breakfast: Slow riverside breakfast in Kampot — eggs, fresh fruit, Khmer iced coffee. ~$4–6.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near the Russian Market or at the airport — banh mi or rice dish. ~$3–6.
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or a farewell meal at a Phnom Penh restaurant if time allows — try Khmer Surin for authentic northeastern Khmer cuisine. ~$8–12 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for Phnom Penh Airport check-in and security. The Russian Market is closed on some public holidays — check ahead. This final day wraps up a beautifully balanced trip: ancient temples, sobering history, vibrant city life, colonial river towns, and pristine beaches — the full Cambodian experience.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to your boutique stay in the Angkor Archaeological Park area. Check-in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome drink and orientation briefing with your personal concierge. Take a leisurely stroll through the hotel grounds and nearby village lanes to acclimatize to the surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the hotel's rooftop or garden terrace overlooking the Cambodian countryside. Enjoy a private welcome dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant featuring refined Khmer cuisine with a contemporary twist.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the hotel upon arrival — fresh tropical fruits, Cambodian spring rolls, and iced jasmine tea
meals.dinner: Private welcome dinner at the hotel's fine-dining restaurant — Amok Trey (coconut fish curry), Lok Lak beef tenderloin, and mango sticky rice for dessert, paired with Cambodian craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Request a late check-out briefing with your private guide to plan the week ahead. Ensure passports and Angkor passes are arranged through the concierge this evening for early temple access the following days.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn private sunrise experience at Angkor Wat — arrive before 5:30 AM to secure the best reflection pool vantage point. Enjoy a curated breakfast picnic basket prepared by the hotel, sipping coffee as the temple emerges from the mist. Private expert guide provides in-depth historical and architectural commentary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the outer galleries of Angkor Wat in detail — the Churning of the Ocean of Milk bas-relief, the Hall of Echoes, and the central sanctuary towers. After lunch, visit Angkor Thom, including the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon, and the Terrace of the Elephants.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a traditional Khmer herbal bath and one-hour signature massage at the spa. Dinner at a premium restaurant in Siem Reap's heritage quarter.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn picnic basket from the hotel — freshly baked croissants, tropical fruit, Cambodian iced coffee, and yogurt
meals.lunch: Private al fresco lunch at a shaded rest pavilion near Angkor Thom — chef-prepared cold mezze, Khmer sandwiches, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Cuisine Wat Damnak or Malis Restaurant, Siem Reap — tasting menu of seasonal Cambodian dishes with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing and comfortable walking shoes. The Angkor complex is vast — a private air-conditioned vehicle with driver is recommended between temple clusters. November weather is ideal — dry and mild.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to Ta Prohm — the iconic jungle temple where ancient tree roots embrace stone corridors. Arrive early to experience it before tour groups arrive. Your guide will share the history of the Rajavihara monastery and its role in the Khmer Empire.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Banteay Kdei and the serene Srah Srang reservoir — a royal bathing pool dating to the 12th century. Followed by a visit to Banteay Srei, the 'Citadel of Women,' renowned for its intricate pink sandstone carvings — considered the jewel of Khmer art.
day_by_day.evening: Attend an exclusive private Apsara dance performance — a UNESCO-recognized classical Khmer art form — arranged at a heritage venue or within the hotel grounds. Post-performance dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the hotel — eggs Benedict with Kampot pepper hollandaise, fresh papaya, Cambodian baguette, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium countryside restaurant near Banteay Srei — grilled river fish, green mango salad, and palm sugar desserts
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner at the hotel garden or a heritage villa restaurant — five-course Khmer tasting menu with sommelier-selected wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is approximately 25 km north of Siem Reap — factor in 40-minute drive each way. The private Apsara performance should be booked at least 48 hours in advance through your concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the lesser-known but spectacular Preah Khan temple — a sprawling monastic complex with long colonnaded corridors, hidden courtyards, and a two-story Hellenistic pavilion. Enjoy an immersive private tour with an archaeologist guide. Followed by Neak Pean, an artificial island temple in the middle of a sacred lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Royal Enclosure area — Phimeanakas (the celestial palace), the Terrace of the Leper King, and the hidden carvings beneath the Baphuon. Afternoon at leisure — return to the hotel for a pool session or spa treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset boat cruise on Tonlé Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia. Champagne and canapés on board as the sun sets over the floating villages.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Khmer rice porridge (Bobor) with ginger and century egg, fresh juices, and pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at a refined riverside restaurant in Siem Reap — Cambodian seafood platter, lotus stem salad, and chilled lemongrass tea
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium floating restaurant on Tonlé Sap or at Siem Reap's top-rated fine dining venue — grilled Mekong lobster, Khmer curry, and tropical sorbet

day_by_day.notes: The Tonlé Sap sunset cruise is best arranged for approximately 17:00–18:30 in November. Bring insect repellent for the lake excursion. The boat should be a private chartered vessel, not a shared tour.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Koh Ker — an ancient remote temple complex that served as the Khmer capital in the 10th century. Arrive by private vehicle (approximately 2-hour drive). Explore the towering seven-tiered pyramid of Prasat Thom and surrounding jungle temples virtually untouched by tourism.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Beng Mealea — a vast, largely unrestored jungle temple that feels like a true archaeological discovery. Wander through collapsed galleries, hidden chambers, and tree-root-entangled towers with your private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap. Relax at the hotel with a sunset cocktail. Dinner at one of Siem Reap's most celebrated chef-driven restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Early packed gourmet breakfast from the hotel — smoked salmon bagels, granola, fruit, and thermos of coffee for the road
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the shade of Beng Mealea — charcuterie, artisan cheeses, Cambodian rice dishes, and fresh fruit prepared by the hotel kitchen
meals.dinner: Dinner at Embassy Restaurant or Tigre de Papier, Siem Reap — contemporary European-Khmer fusion with craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Koh Ker and Beng Mealea make for a long but rewarding full-day excursion. Depart by 7:00 AM. Wear sturdy shoes for uneven temple ruins. Bring sun protection and ample water.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive cultural morning — visit the Artisans Angkor workshop and showroom to witness master craftspeople carving sandstone, silk weaving, and lacquerware painting using techniques passed down through generations. Private guided tour with a cultural historian.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Angkor National Museum for a curated private tour — 1,000 years of Khmer civilization presented through exquisite artifacts, including the Gallery of a Thousand Buddhas. Followed by a cooking class at a premium culinary school — learn to prepare three classic Khmer dishes with a professional chef.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Siem Reap night scene — a private guided walk through the Old French Quarter, Pub Street area (from a cultural perspective), and the night market. Conclude with a premium cocktail experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — French toast with palm sugar syrup, seasonal fruit platter, cold-pressed juices, and specialty Cambodian robusta coffee
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class as your lunch
meals.dinner: Dinner at Haven Restaurant (social enterprise supporting at-risk youth) or Sugar Palm Restaurant — authentic Khmer family recipes elevated to fine dining

day_by_day.notes: Artisans Angkor purchases directly support Cambodian artisans — an excellent place for premium, ethically sourced souvenirs and gifts. The cooking class should be pre-booked through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter transfer from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (approximately 45 minutes) — aerial views of the Tonlé Sap floodplains and Mekong Delta. Check in at a luxury hotel in Phnom Penh (e.g., Rosewood Phnom Penh or Raffles Hotel Le Royal).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the spiritual and ceremonial heart of Cambodia. Admire the Throne Hall, Napoleon III Pavilion, and the emerald Buddha. Followed by the National Museum of Cambodia — home to the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the confluence of the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers (Chaktomuk). Dinner at a premier Phnom Penh restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Siem Reap before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riverside fine-dining restaurant in Phnom Penh — Mekong river prawns, Cambodian beef lok lak, and fresh coconut dessert
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Phnom Penh or Topaz Restaurant — French-Cambodian cuisine with an exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter transfer must be booked well in advance. Alternatively, a premium private car transfer (approximately 6 hours) or domestic flight can be arranged. Modest dress required for Royal Palace visit — shoulders and knees must be covered.

day_by_day.morning: Sobering but essential cultural experience — a private guided visit to Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) and the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial. A deeply moving and important historical journey into Cambodia's 20th-century tragedy, guided by a knowledgeable historian.
day_by_day.afternoon: Recovery and reflection time — explore the elegant Psar Thmei (Central Market) art deco building and the upscale boutiques of BKK1 neighborhood for premium Cambodian crafts, silk, and contemporary art galleries. Visit Wat Phnom — the hilltop temple at the heart of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset cruise on the Mekong River aboard a chartered traditional wooden boat — champagne, fresh oysters, and canapés as the city lights come alive. Followed by dinner at the hotel's fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte hotel breakfast — eggs your way, smoked duck, fresh tropical fruits, Cambodian rice porridge, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Khéma Pasteur or The Chinese House — premium café fare with Cambodian and French influences in a beautiful colonial setting
meals.dinner: Private dinner on the Mekong cruise boat or at the hotel's signature restaurant — seven-course degustation menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visit is emotionally intense — allow time for quiet reflection afterward. Audio guides and private guides are both available; a private guide provides the most contextual depth.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight or helicopter transfer from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (approximately 45 minutes), then speedboat transfer to Koh Rong Samloem or Song Saa Private Island — Cambodia's premier luxury island destination. Check in to an overwater villa or beachfront suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon of pure relaxation — snorkeling in the crystal-clear Gulf of Thailand waters, kayaking through mangrove channels, or simply unwinding on your private stretch of white sand beach. Optional guided reef snorkeling tour with a marine biologist.
day_by_day.evening: Barefoot luxury beach dinner — private table set on the sand with tiki torches, fresh seafood barbecue, and chilled rosé. Stargazing session with the resort's astronomy guide.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Phnom Penh before departure
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the island resort — grilled lobster, tropical ceviche, and fresh coconut water served beachside
meals.dinner: Private beach barbecue dinner — whole grilled snapper, tiger prawns, Cambodian seafood curry, and tropical fruit platter with champagne

day_by_day.notes: Song Saa Private Island and Koh Rong Samloem's Lazy Beach area offer Cambodia's finest island luxury. Book island accommodation well in advance — November is peak season. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect marine ecosystems.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the island — sunrise yoga session on the beach or a guided jungle trek through the island's protected forest reserve. Last swim and snorkel in the turquoise waters. Leisurely breakfast overlooking the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Speedboat transfer back to the mainland, then private vehicle or charter flight to Phnom Penh International Airport or Siem Reap International Airport for departure. En route, stop for a final Cambodian coffee and souvenir shopping at a curated artisan store.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cambodia — farewell to a kingdom of wonder, history, and breathtaking natural beauty.

meals.breakfast: Final island breakfast — tropical fruit bowls, freshly baked pastries, eggs Benedict, and specialty coffee with ocean views
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at an airport lounge or premium restaurant near the departure airport — Cambodian noodle soup, spring rolls, and fresh lychee juice
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at the connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3–4 hours from island departure to airport check-in, accounting for boat transfer and road/air travel. Confirm all departure logistics the night before with your concierge. Consider purchasing premium Cambodian silk, Kampot pepper, and Artisans Angkor pieces as final gifts.
